reasoning: Brian Chu notes that while Newmont is the world's largest gold miner and would naturally generate the most absolute cash, he cautions against using absolute cash figures as a quality measure. He instead applies a standardised operating margin metric he developed, which measures the spread between gold selling price and all-in sustaining costs divided by the average quarterly gold price rather than the company's own realised price. This approach penalises companies that hedge below spot gold prices. On this basis, he does not regard Newmont as the standout performer despite UBS's buy rating and $180 target.
quote: Well, I believe they do have the data. And Newmont Mining being the largest gold mining company, you would expect that they would deliver the most, um, generate the most cash. So I would actually measure it using the standardised operating margin, which I developed myself. I would look at the difference between what the company is, uh, earning, selling their gold, how much they, um, they incur for the all in sustaining costs. And rather than dividing it by the cost of selling the gold for themselves. I'm actually standardizing it by saying, what is the average quarterly price for gold during this quarter?
